written.myAnswer: The cell membrane forms the boundary of the cell and selectively controls the movement of substances into and out of it.
The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts and packages materials—especially proteins from the rough ER—into vesicles for use in the cell or transport outside it.
Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that digest food and break down cellular wastes and worn-out or damaged organelles.
Smooth ER is involved in lipid metabolism, intracellular transport and detoxification. In muscle cells, specialized smooth ER stores calcium ions needed for muscle contraction.
Most mature plant cells have one large central vacuole containing cell sap. Animal cells generally have smaller, often temporary vacuoles.
Cristae increase the inner surface area of mitochondria, providing more area for the reactions of cellular respiration.
Chromatin consists of DNA and proteins. When a cell divides, it condenses to form visible chromosomes.

(a) Cell membrane: lipids and proteins, with a small amount of carbohydrate. (b) Fungal cell wall: chitin. (c) Plant cell wall: mainly cellulose, with other substances such as hemicellulose and pectin; secondary walls may also contain lignin. (d) Bacterial cell wall: peptidoglycan. (e) Ribosomes: rRNA and proteins. (f) Chromosomes: DNA and proteins.

The fluid mosaic model describes a cell membrane as a fluid lipid bilayer with proteins embedded in or associated with it. Lipids and many proteins can move laterally, giving the membrane a changing mosaic pattern. Carbohydrates may be attached to proteins or lipids.

The cell wall is a rigid, non-living layer outside the cell membrane. It gives the cell shape, support and protection. In plants it includes the middle lamella, primary wall and, in some cells, secondary wall. Plasmodesmata connect adjacent plant cells and allow materials to pass between them.

The nucleus is enclosed by a double-membraned nuclear envelope with pores. Its nucleoplasm contains nucleoli and chromatin, which consists of DNA and proteins and condenses into chromosomes during cell division. The nucleolus is involved in ribosome formation, and DNA genes control cell activities and carry hereditary information.

Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicles containing digestive enzymes; they digest food and break down cellular wastes and worn-out organelles. The endoplasmic reticulum is a network of membrane-bound channels. Rough ER has ribosomes and is involved in protein synthesis, while smooth ER lacks ribosomes and is involved in lipid metabolism, transport and detoxification.

Chloroplasts are green, double-membrane-bound plastids containing chlorophyll. Inside, thylakoids are arranged in stacks called grana and are surrounded by stroma. Chloroplasts contain DNA and ribosomes and carry out photosynthesis, using light energy to make glucose.

Mitochondrial dysfunction or absence would reduce ATP production by aerobic respiration. As a result, energy-dependent processes in other organelles, including synthesis, transport and cellular maintenance, could slow down or fail.
